questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to visit Australia and thought this was the perfect opportunity. It was important for me to go to an English speaking country and a great university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Really easy - the university did a great job!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not so easy. I found a share house on a Facebook page called fairyfloss. I lived in a beautiful house with three roommates all from Australia. I would definitely recommend that option!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Melbourne is huge. I spend a lot of time on transportation although I also think I got a good understanding of the different parts of the city that I would not have had had I lived near campus. That said, it was frustrating having to go home early and say no to stuff going on in the city because I was unable to get back home.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Pretty straightforward. Just make sure you have approval for the final courses you select.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop 1 was a place on campus you could go with any question you may have.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: First week of the semester you are not locked into any courses. It’s a week of shopping and seeing if the courses you have selected are for you, and if not you have time to try other courses as well. That worked really great and I ended up  changing most of my courses. The ones I ended up with were perfect for me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It’s a great school and an amazing opportunity!

questions.answer: Year 1 is very easy. Year 3 can be a bit tough depending on what you select. I would recommend mixing year 2 and 3.

questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Entrepreneurship for sustainability is a great course for meeting other students. Through the course you work in a dedicated team of 5 or so. So at the end you know those people pretty well. It’s also just a great course!
International Macro 
economics is a great course as well thought by an amazing professor!
